summary: The note argues that AI integration is becoming essential for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), which have historically driven innovation but adopted AI more cautiously than big corporations. It covers the September 2023 report that spurred interest, current uses in CRM, supply chain, marketing and operations, and the view that AI complements the human workforce. It also gives advice on strategic investment and describes government support such as the "AI for SMEs" grant.
one_line: SMEs are increasingly adopting AI in CRM, supply chain, marketing and operations, aided by grants, strategic investment and employee training.
key_facts: A groundbreaking report published on September 15, 2023, co-authored by Dr. Helen Cho and Mark Richardson, prompted SMEs to seriously consider AI.
The report's case studies of early adopters showed substantial growth in customer satisfaction and profitability.
As of late 2023, AI implementation in SMEs is more widespread due to increased accessibility and more service providers catering to smaller businesses.
Current SME-focused AI applications are ones that do not require large datasets to function effectively.
AI-powered CRM systems can predict customer behavior, automate communications and offer personalized experiences.
A case study from October 2023 showed that "AI Smart Stock" software reduced inventory costs by 25% for a small retailer.

Sarah Thompson, a digital marketing expert, said in a November 6, 2023 webinar that AI-enabled ad platforms helped small businesses double their reach without proportionately increasing marketing budgets.
Michael Anderson, an AI ethics consultant, stated in a September 28, 2023 panel discussion that employee training is crucial so SME staff can work alongside AI.
Natalie Keen, a tech consultant, recommends starting with AI tools that address immediate business challenges and avoiding over-investment.
Keen has observed an uptick in adoption of AI business analytics tools that let SMEs decide without a full data analytics department.
The government introduced the "AI for SMEs" grant on September 20, 2023, covering part of the costs of procuring AI tools and services.
On-demand AI services, which require no significant initial investment, are expected to accelerate AI adoption among SMEs.
